reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes the demons' fearful assent to facts about Christ from the loving, obedient faith that truly marks one as born of God.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll, Strauss, and Schweitzer's survey of Wrede all press the same point: demons meet the Gospels' own confession test for knowing Christ, yet plainly are not born of God.

quotes.text: "Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God." … I believe it is stated in the Bible that "the very devils believe;" and it would seem from this that belief is not such a meritorious thing, after all.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III, The Works of Robert G. Ingersoll, Vol. VI (Dresden Edition, 1900), on James 2:19 and 1 John 5:1.

quotes.text: he should have the involuntary homage of demons, whose testimony, since they had only ruin to expect from him, must be impartial, and from their higher spiritual nature was to be relied on.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), § 93, on James 2:19 and 1 John 5:1.

quotes.text: How do the demoniacs know that Jesus is the Son of God?
quotes.attr: Albert Schweitzer (d. 1965), The Quest of the Historical Jesus, trans. W. Montgomery (1910), ch. II, on James 2:19 and 1 John 5:1.

sides.snippet: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe, and shudder.
sides.verseText: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe, and shudder.

sides.snippet: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.
sides.verseText: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. Whoever loves the father also loves the child who is born of him.
